subject: Dedicated capacity guarantee onboarding: measurement checklist & benchmark scripts
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity guarantee onboarding: measurement checklist & benchmark scripts

Hi Asha / Ben —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our call, I wanted to share the recommended acceptance workflow we use when customers onboard Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and request throughput guarantees. The goal is to make the measurement deterministic so your SREs can validate tokens/sec and percentile latency without surprises.

Quick summary of the proposed approach (attached script + short test window):
- Week 0: baseline profiling (light traffic) to capture seq-length distribution and token mix.
- Week 1: controlled acceptance test — 30 min steady-state run at target QPS with the Redwood benchmark scripts (attached).
- Measurements: 95th token-latency, tail (>99th) single-request latency, sustained tokens/sec and successful request% over the window.
- Pass criteria: sustained >= agreed tokens/sec for 95% of 1-min samples and p95 latency <= agreed threshold.

I attached the benchmark scripts and a small workbook for you to drop in your sample payloads. Marcus is looping in sizing guidance if we need to expand the pool for burst tolerance.

Ask: can your team run the attached script during a 30-minute acceptance window next Wednesday (May 19) or Friday (May 21)? If you want different timing, propose a slot and we’ll confirm.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick runbook walk-through if helpful.

—Irene
Irene Choi

Hi Asha —

Quick note from sizing/engineering: commit bands are defined by reserved GPU pool size (e.g., 8-GPU, 16-GPU) and the model variant you plan to serve. For DEAL-4532 I modeled two realistic bands:

- Band A (8-GPU pool): baseline sustained ~1.2M tokens/sec for 512-token average sequences, p95 latency <= 180ms for single-stream requests.
- Band B (16-GPU pool): baseline sustained ~2.4M tokens/sec, p95 latency <= 120ms.

Important caveat: these numbers assume the same model quantization profile and no additional third-party latency (e.g., customer-side network shaping). We recommend the acceptance test run with your production-ish input mix (Asha's samples).

If Band A is what you expect to purchase, Redwood can guarantee the tokens/sec figure in the contract for the agreed traffic profile and offer a 12% commit discount at annual billing. For Band B we can extend a 18% commit discount. Discounts are indexed to committed pool size and a 3-month ramp window.

I’ll attach a short acceptance-run checklist and the scripts to be executed. Laura, please confirm pricing language and whether we need a special clause for burst headroom.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

Hi all —

Thanks — looping in pricing/ops notes. A couple of contract-level points to flag:

- We can include a dedicated throughput SLA clause that references the acceptance-run results (tokens/sec + p95 latency) and ties it to the committed pool size. SLA credits will be tiered: 1% credit for >=98% of target, 3% credit for 95–97%, subject to a max quarterly cap.
- Discounts (12% / 18%) are contingent on a 12-month minimum commit and upfront payment terms (net 30).
- We prefer to avoid guaranteeing headroom for unprofiled burst traffic; instead we provide a documented burst policy (pre-negotiated burst credits or short-term burst add-ons).

Ben / Asha: if those commercial terms are acceptable, we’ll prepare the draft SLA wording (attached draft) and a short appendix that includes the acceptance-run data format.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Irene / Marcus / Laura —

Appreciate the detail. Procurement is comfortable with the proposed acceptance window this Friday (May 21). Two notes from our legal/ops:

1) We need the SLA to explicitly list the measurement method (the exact script name and the Drive link) and say the acceptance run must be executed from an IP range we provide.
2) On discounts: we can accept the 12% / 18% tiering but request a one-time additional onboarding credit (equivalent to 1 month of committed spend) if the acceptance run fails due to Redwood-side regression.

Assuming those two items are added to the draft we’ll sign the 12-month commit for Band A. We’ll pull together the IP range and sample production keys for the run.

—Ben
